title: Service runway forecast and risk debrief
summary: Quarterly operational check: review of usage trends, a recent cost spike, latency regressions on p95 for chat endpoints, and runway scenarios for the pilot. Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, VPC connectivity concerns, and a small security ask around KMS/HSM key rotation. Agreed next steps for pricing scenarios, benchmark window, and an on-prem connectivity diagram.
action_items: Alex Kim - send 3 runway pricing scenarios (3/6/12 month commits) with clear #s for dedicated capacity vs hosted - 2025-10-07
Priya Nair - run a focused p95 latency benchmark on current model (dialogue-003) with sample payloads from Bluefront; include kv-cache and batching toggles - 2025-10-06
Samir Patel - share representative traffic traces and top 20 prompt lengths to help batching/caching tuning - 2025-10-04
Lena Huang - provide network diagram and firewall egress rules for VPC peering attempt; list times maintenance windows - 2025-10-09
Jordan Li - schedule follow-up pilot kickoff and internal security review handoff call - 2025-10-10
next_steps: Redwood to propose pricing + capacity scenarios
SE benchmark and share results with traces and config recommendations
Customer to provide traffic traces and VPC diagram
Follow-up call scheduled for 2025-10-13 to pick decision path
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Kim: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we got about an hour — we'll run through the usage and the cost spike, then priya will talk benchmarks and options.
[00:08] Maria Gomez: thanks Alex, appreciate it. quick ask up front, finance wants a 6 week runway if we ramp to prod — need to know cost burn, so that's why we flagged today.
[00:22] Alex Kim: totally, that's the goal. quick roll call?
[00:26] Samir Patel: samir here, ml infra, hi.
[00:29] Lena Huang: lena, s-r-e.
[00:31] Priya Nair: priya from redwood se.
[00:33] Jordan Li: jordan, customer success.
[00:36] Alex Kim: alright — two quick slides, then open. first: usage trend, bluefront's token growth is steady but we saw a daily spike last week (around oct 24) that doubled hourly tps on chat route.
[00:51] Maria Gomez: yes that spike correlated with a campaign, but we thought the platform should have absorbed it; cost jumped 2.3x that day — billing flagged it.
[01:02] Priya Nair: looking at the traces you shared, there's a long tail of prompt sizes — lots of 5–6k token prompts now, which increases kv cache pressure and the effective compute per request. also we saw fewer cache hits because of slight prompt template drift.
[01:18] Samir Patel: prompt drift, hmm — we updated templates but didn't re-run eval; could have introduced more variable context.
[01:24] Lena Huang: network wise, we also had retries between app and redwood during that window, not sure if egress was rate-limited by our firewall.
[01:33] Alex Kim: that combination explains cost. retried requests + longer sequences + lower cache hit = more token compute.
[01:40] Maria Gomez: what's the quick mitigation? can we cap prompt lengths or set batching?
[01:45] Priya Nair: immediate ops: enable prefix/KV cache for the chat route and set a soft prompt length ceiling in the client, maybe 3k for now. medium-term: batching and config changes in the SE layer. also quantization recommendation might drop p50 cost.
[01:58] Samir Patel: curious about p95 latency — our product team flagged p95 regressions after the template change.
[02:04] Priya Nair: right — p95 jumped from 280ms to ~420ms on that day for the streaming endpoint. we suspect KV cache churn and the higher variance in sequence length caused the runtime to pick less optimal kernels.
[02:18] Alex Kim: we can run a focused benchmark with representative traces; priya you'll run that and include caching and continuous-batch settings?
[02:26] Priya Nair: yes, i'll run with dialog-model-003 (approx config you used) and test three batch sizes, and include quantized variant. i'll also surface token-level time breakdowns.
[02:36] Maria Gomez: is the quantized model going to change quality? we can't degrade user experience.
[02:40] Priya Nair: small chance for some hallucination differences; we'll include quality checks using your existing eval set. if we see regressions we'll propose a rollout plan with canaries.
[02:49] Samir Patel: on dedicated vs hosted — we keep hearing mixed advice. our security team leans private. cost team leans hosted for lower ops. what's the tradeoff in immediate latency and cost predictability?
[03:00] Alex Kim: quick summary: hosted lets you scale instantly and pay per token — good for variable traffic. Dedicated gives predictable throughput/SLOs and often lower unit cost at high commit levels, plus isolation, VPC options. but there's commit/capacity lead time.
[03:15] Maria Gomez: can you show an example math for 6 week runway?
[03:19] Alex Kim: yes — i'll produce three scenarios: self-serve hosted with burst, modest dedicated commit (x GPUs), and a higher commit for 12 month. we'll show per-token unit cost and a burn chart for 6 weeks.
[03:30] Lena Huang: on VPC peering — we tried to set up a connection but saw cert handshake failures; we'd like an on-prem diagram to show port ranges and ip blocks.
[03:40] Priya Nair: we'll pull the network doc and outline the typical egress rules and peering steps; for some customers we do a private control plane + customer managed data path, which avoids our control plane seeing payloads.
[03:52] Samir Patel: depends on compliance — we need SOC2 plus proof that keys never leave our KMS. we use HSM-backed keys.
[03:59] Alex Kim: we can provide our compliance pack and KMS integration notes — our private deployment supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit logs. we'll surface the sequence for key rotation and attestations.
[04:10] Maria Gomez: perfect. also need SSO/SAML and RBAC mapping for our team.
[04:15] Jordan Li: noted — we'll include SSO docs.
[04:17] Maria Gomez: timeline: we'd like to make a decision by mid-october to hit the campaign window.
[04:22] Alex Kim: ok — decision checkpoint 2025-10-13 per earlier note. we'll prepare the cost scenarios and benchmark by next week.
[04:30] Priya Nair: one more technical note — if you decide on dedicated we recommend a canary rollout with 10% traffic first to validate early at production scale; we can fully instrument token breakdowns and error budgets.
[04:44] Samir Patel: what's the expected delta p95 improvement on dedicated? is it network or runtime bound?
[04:50] Priya Nair: usually dedicated reduces p95 by ~15-35% if contention was the issue; run your traces through the benchmark to confirm. sometimes network egress or retry patterns dominate, so we need the traces to know.
[05:05] Lena Huang: ok samir will send traces and we'll try to reproduce the firewall behavior.
[05:10] Alex Kim: i'll compile the three pricing scenarios and include a simple decision matrix: cost, latency, isolation, lead time. also will include rough pilot acceptance criteria.
[05:20] Maria Gomez: any blockers on the security side for us?
[05:23] Jordan Li: we need to get redwood's SOC2 and KMS integration notes, and a short note on audit logs retention.
[05:31] Alex Kim: that's doable. we'll also include contact for the private deployment engineer.
[05:36] Maria Gomez: great.
[05:38] Alex Kim: quick recap of agreed actions...
[05:42] Jordan Li: (talking over) recap — redwood pricing scenarios, se bench, customer traces, vpc diagram, security docs, follow-up 10-13.
[05:50] Alex Kim: yep. thanks all, we'll follow up via email with artifacts. meeting adjourned.
